# agent-config

> Short Agent Skills for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi): the agent asks once, then does reversible work and reports what it decided. Every rule traces to a failure someone saw, logged in FAILURES.md.

Install all skills, not a subset: they hand off to each other by name, and `working-style` carries the always-on rule.

## Start here

- [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md): steps for an agent to install, verify, update and remove the skills
- [skills.json](skills.json): index of every skill with its description, stage, failure fixed and startup cost
- [FAILURES.md](FAILURES.md): per skill, the failure it fixes and where that failure was seen
- [evals/README.md](evals/README.md): behaviour tests in the `claude plugin eval` format, and how to run them

## Skills

<!-- skills-list:start (generated by scripts/build-index.mjs from skills/; do not edit) -->
- [brainstorm](skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md): Think a new project through with the user before anything is built. Interview them for intent, research in the background, converge on a direction, and write the design. Use for "brainstorm", "let's brainstorm", "new project", or starting a product from scratch.
- [grilling](skills/grilling/SKILL.md): Stress-test a plan, decision or idea through rounds of pointed questions, each with a recommended answer. Use for "grill me", "poke holes in this", "challenge my plan", or when a design must converge on decisions.
- [research](skills/research/SKILL.md): Investigate a defined question against primary sources and return a cited, dated answer. Use for "research X", "find out", docs or API facts, comparing options, or as a background lane for another skill; not for plain codebase explanation (explain-codebase).
- [prototype](skills/prototype/SKILL.md): Build a throwaway artifact to settle one uncertain design question. Use for "prototype", "spike", "mockup", "try a few versions", "does this state model feel right", or "what should this look like". Skip when the behavior is already settled.
- [writing-plans](skills/writing-plans/SKILL.md): Turn an approved design or clear requirements into an implementation plan of small, independently testable tasks with exact files, interfaces and checks. Use for "write a plan", "plan this out", or before multi-step work.
- [to-issues](skills/to-issues/SKILL.md): Break a design, plan or conversation into tracer-bullet issues with blocking edges, then publish them to GitHub Issues, Linear, or Markdown files (Obsidian-friendly). Use for "break this into issues", "create tickets", "make a backlog", "put this in Linear/GitHub".
- [architecture-design](skills/architecture-design/SKILL.md): Design or reshape a module, interface, seam, or subsystem before coding, or restructure existing code without changing behavior. Use for "design this", "architect", "refactor", "restructure", extract/move/rename/dedupe, or unclear ownership; skip routine edits that fit an established shape.
- [implement](skills/implement/SKILL.md): Execute an approved plan or set of issues to completion, task by task, with tests, verification and review. Use for "implement this", "build the plan", "work the issues", "start on ticket X".
- [working-style](skills/working-style/SKILL.md): Proceed, then present: do reversible work, report why. Ask only about product direction, or before irreversible or outward-facing steps: force-push, shared merge, deleting data, publishing, messaging people.
- [orchestrate](skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md): Run a long session as the coordinator of implementer and reviewer agents working tickets in parallel worktrees, under the user's standing orders. Use for "orchestrate", "run the factory", "work the backlog", "keep agents busy", or any session that dispatches many implementers.
- [test-driven-development](skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md): Build features and fix bugs test-first with red-green-refactor at agreed seams. Use for TDD, "write a failing test first", regression tests, or any behavior change with a testable seam.
- [systematic-debugging](skills/systematic-debugging/SKILL.md): Find the root cause of bugs, test failures, regressions, flaky or slow behavior before fixing. Use for "debug this", "diagnose", "why does X fail", anything broken, throwing, or slow, and before proposing any fix.
- [frontend-design](skills/frontend-design/SKILL.md): Design and build web UI that avoids template and AI-generated looks. Use when building or restyling pages, components, dashboards, or landing pages, when asked to "make it look good", and when UX flows, information architecture, or screen states need deciding first.
- [verification-before-completion](skills/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md): Gate any claim that work is done, fixed, passing, or ready on fresh evidence. Use right before saying "done", "fixed", or "passing", handing work back, committing, or opening a PR.
- [create-verification-skill](skills/create-verification-skill/SKILL.md): Write a project's own verify-<app> skill that tells any agent how to launch the app from scratch, drive a feature like a user, capture evidence and clean up. Use for "make a verification skill", "how do agents prove changes work here", or when agents keep claiming done without running the app.
- [code-review](skills/code-review/SKILL.md): Review a diff, branch, PR, or files for spec and standards fit, and trace what a change could break beyond the diff. Use for "review this", "what could this break", "blast radius", or when acting on review feedback.
- [ci-pr-lifecycle](skills/ci-pr-lifecycle/SKILL.md): Check or drive a branch, PR, and CI through to a finished state. Use for "is this ready", "CI status", "open a PR", "push and watch CI", "retry the failed job", or finishing a branch. Never merges without an explicit ask.
- [explain-codebase](skills/explain-codebase/SKILL.md): Explain how existing code works, and when asked why it is shaped that way. Use for "how does X work", walkthroughs, "where should this live", "why is this here", and design rationale. Read-only.
- [wait-what](skills/wait-what/SKILL.md): Re-pitch your last message when it did not land. Use when the user is confused by your previous answer: "wait, what", "explain that normally", "I don't get it", "in plain English". One turn; no research.
- [handoff](skills/handoff/SKILL.md): Write a handoff brief for another agent, session, or machine, or resume work from one. Use for "hand off", "write a handoff", "pick up where we left off", "take over from this brief or branch".
- [reflect](skills/reflect/SKILL.md): Mine the current session for durable lessons and turn each into a concrete edit to a skill, an AGENTS.md, or an enforcement backlog item. Use for "reflect", "what did we learn", "update the skills from this session", or after a session full of corrections.
- [technical-documentation](skills/technical-documentation/SKILL.md): Write or revise source-grounded docs: READMEs, tutorials, how-to guides, references, explanations, design docs, and user guides or SOPs for non-technical operators. Use when documentation must be accurate, scannable, and verified against the current system.
- [unslop](skills/unslop/SKILL.md): Remove AI tells from prose while keeping facts and voice. Use as the final pass on reports, docs, READMEs, proposals, PR descriptions, and posts, or when asked to humanize, tighten, or de-slop text. Skip code, logs, quotes, and short chat replies.
<!-- skills-list:end -->
